title: OM scalable crossover profiling
objective: Profile scalable higher-order OM workloads and source-transparently accelerate the exact polynomial and MaxMin loops enough to establish a measured crossover boundary without changing public selection

oracles: SageMath/PARI exact maximal-order discriminant and index

handoff.summary: The follow-up reduces degree-one residual extensions exactly to the certified F_p[x] factorizer and accelerates the independent exhaustive MaxMin checker with common-denominator integer valuations while reconstructing only selected numerators. On v429/p=7 the same certificate is complete with local index 480: CPython falls from 6.65s to 1.09s and Sage.js from a 45s timeout to 23.16s. Opt-in scalable and v429 benchmark profiles preserve certificate identifiers and state explicitly that p=2 local timings are not comparable to full-global PARI/Hecke timings.
risks: The complete Sage.js v429/p=7 certificate remains about 21 times slower than CPython and is not an end-to-end crossover against PARI.
Higher nonlinear residual extensions at v429 primes 2, 3, and 5 still fail closed; p=59 hits the bounded factor-candidate resource limit.
Full bad-generator index factorization exceeded the bounded oracle timeout and belongs to discriminant-component orchestration rather than this local OM lane.
next_steps: Keep public auto-selection disabled: direct PARI nfbasis remains faster and the measured OM stress rows are local-only.
Add scalable higher residual-field factorization to cover the v429 p=2,3,5 boundary without weakening fail-closed evidence.
Profile the remaining 11s Sage.js exhaustive integer-valuation loop before considering a same-source native lowering.
